title: Chemistry Myths
objective: After this level you can debunk myths, like "chemical-free" products.
summary: Everything is made of chemicals, so nothing is chemical-free: a 2008 million-pound offer and a blank 2014 'overview' made the point. And a molecule is the same from fruit or factory.

cards.headline: In 2008, chemists offered a million pounds for anything 100% chemical-free.
cards.body: The Royal Society of Chemistry promised the money to the first member of the public who could hand over such a material. Why were they so relaxed about it?

cards.headline: Everything is chemicals
cards.body: Everything you eat, drink and live in is made of chemicals, natural and synthetic alike. Level 2 said matter is anything with mass that takes up space, and Level 1 said chemistry studies what matter is made of. A truly chemical-free product would have to be made of nothing at all. The Royal Society of Chemistry was reclaiming the word from advertising, where chemical had come to mean poison.

mascot.line: The word to rethink: chemical doesn't mean poison. Everything you eat and drink is chemicals.

cards.headline: A paper with nothing in it
cards.body: In 2014 two chemists sent the journal Nature Chemistry "A comprehensive overview of chemical-free consumer products". They examined lotions, supplements, household cleaners, foods and drinks, then listed every product that truly deserved the label. The list was empty. The journal shared the paper on its blog.

cards.headline: Natural isn't a different molecule
cards.body: A related myth says synthetic versions are chemically different from natural ones. Vitamin C says otherwise: natural and synthetic vitamin C are chemically identical, with no known difference in how they act in your body. A molecule doesn't remember whether it came from fruit or a factory. What matters is which substance it is, not where it was made.
cards.callout: Same molecule, same chemistry, whatever the label says.

cards.headline: Myths: busted
learned: Everything is made of chemicals, natural and synthetic
Natural and synthetic vitamin C are the same molecule
What matters is the substance, not where it came from

questions.prompt: In 2014, what did the "comprehensive overview of chemical-free consumer products" list?

options.label: Every product sold in health food shops

questions.explanation: After examining lotions, supplements, cleaners, foods and drinks, the authors found no truly chemical-free products.

questions.prompt: Is vitamin C made in a factory chemically different from vitamin C in fruit?

options.label: Yes: synthetic vitamin C is a different molecule
No: natural and synthetic vitamin C are chemically identical
Yes: only natural vitamin C works in the body
options.rationale: There's no known difference in how they act.

options.label: It depends on the color of the tablet
options.rationale: Color has nothing to do with it.

questions.explanation: Natural and synthetic L-ascorbic acid are the same molecule, with no known difference in biological activity.

questions.prompt: A shampoo bottle says "chemical-free". Using Level 2's definition of matter, what's the chemist's correction?

options.label: Only liquids are made of chemicals
options.rationale: Solids and gases are made of chemicals too.

options.label: The shampoo is matter, and all matter is made of chemicals
Shampoo has no mass, so the label is fine
options.rationale: Anything you can pour has mass.

options.label: Only factory-made ingredients count as chemicals

questions.explanation: Shampoo has mass and takes up space, so it's matter, and everything made of matter is made of chemicals.
